messages:
Meera: heads-up — received a DSAR asking for full erasure (user email attached). Looks like there's an active forensic_hold:INC-4521 for a vuln triage that may require data retention. KMS rotation started yesterday too. What's the safe path?
Ajay: which storage locations are we talking about? embeddings, vector DB snapshots, S3 buckets?
Meera: primary: s3://redwood-prod-embeddings-eu, nightly snapshots in eu-west-1, and a few archived snapshots in gs://redwood-archive-eu. Also some derived vectors in our vector service indexes.
Sam: we can't delete if triage needs evidence. Legal needs to sign off. Also need to confirm whether any snapshots are encrypted with an old key that will be rotated.
legal-tilly: @Meera thanks — Legal needs the original DSAR copy + the vuln case id and a list of places where the subject appears. We typically issue a legal hold if triage requires preservation. Can infra add a hold flag and an audit record?
infra-bot: audit log entry created: action=legal_hold_set actor=Meera case=INC-4521 ts=1718894326
Olivia: KMS rotation note: key-rotation job started 1718891200. Some archived snapshots are still queued for re-encryption. If we delete data encrypted under the old key mid-rotation we risk breaking recoverability for the forensic copies. Recommend pausing deletion until rotation completes or exporting a key-wrapped copy for Legal.
Ajay: ops question — can we add a scoped RBAC permission so Legal can flip a release flag without needing infra root keys? Proposed permission: resource:embeddings:manage:delete_confirm granted to team:legal. That would let Legal approve a release while leaving deletes to ops.
Sam: agree in principle, but require the RBAC change to emit an immutable audit event and require 2-person approval for release. Also need to ensure automated purge jobs are blocked for subjects under legal hold.
Meera: I'll draft an RFC and a tiny RBAC PR. Proposed runbook (draft):
``` 
1) Freeze auto-purge for subject_id
2) Create audit entry: legal_hold_set (include case id)
3) Notify security and triage channel #inc-4521
4) Legal initiates release -> requires 2 approvals (legal + security)
5) Ops runs safe-delete job which logs keystamp + deletion_manifest
```
Olivia: addendum: safe-delete should verify KMS key version before removing any encrypted snapshots. Log key-version-id and kms:decrypt call in the audit entry to avoid orphaned ciphertext.
legal-tilly: Legal will not release until triage publishes closure and a signed release. When that happens we'll record the signed release email in the case and flip the release flag. After release, Ops should produce a deletion manifest for the user. :thumbsup:
Ajay: filing JIRA for the RBAC + runbook: SECOPS-7789. @Meera can you be assignee for the initial PR?
Meera: yep, I'll open RFC + PR by EOD tomorrow. If the DSAR is urgent we can create a formal retention-exception with documented justification to temporarily honor the hold.
Sam: tagging infra-bot to create the retention-exception ticket so we have a paper trail.
infra-bot: retention-exception ticket created: RE-7789 assignee=Meera link=https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RE-7789
Meera: thanks all — looping Legal and Infra for follow-ups. Will post RFC link once ready. :eyes:
